questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following reactions will yield a primary amine as the major organic product?
A. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{Na(Hg)} / \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}}$
B. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4}$
C. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{(i) } \text{SnCl}_2 + \text{HCl}}$
D. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2 / \text{Ni}}$
E. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{(i) } \text{LiAlH}_4}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Reaction A: Reduction of an alkyl cyanide with sodium amalgam and ethanol (Mendius reduction) yields a primary amine.
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{Na(Hg)} / \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$

Reaction B: Reduction of an alkyl isocyanide with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields a secondary amine.
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3$

Reaction C: Stephen reduction of an alkyl cyanide yields an aldehyde.
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{(i) } \text{SnCl}_2 + \text{HCl}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$

Reaction D: Catalytic hydrogenation of an alkyl cyanide yields a primary amine.
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2 / \text{Ni}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$

Reaction E: Reduction of an alkyl cyanide with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields a primary amine.
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{(i) } \text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$

Thus, reactions A, D, and E yield primary amines as the major organic product.

Answer: A, D and E only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List I (Catalyst)List II (Process/Reaction)
A$\text{TiCl}_4 + \text{Al(CH}_3\text{)}_3$IOxidation of $\text{HCl}$ to $\text{Cl}_2$
B$\text{CuCl}_2$IIReaction between $\text{I}^-$ and $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$
C$\text{Ni}$IIIHydrogenation of vegetable oils
D$\text{Fe}^{3+}$IVPolymerisation of ethene


Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$\text{TiCl}_4 + \text{Al(CH}_3\text{)}_3$ is the Ziegler-Natta catalyst, which is used for the polymerisation of ethene. Thus, A matches with IV.

$\text{CuCl}_2$ is used as a catalyst in Deacon's process for the oxidation of $\text{HCl}$ to $\text{Cl}_2$. Thus, B matches with I.

Finely divided $\text{Ni}$ is used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils. Thus, C matches with III.

$\text{Fe}^{3+}$ catalyses the reaction between iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) and persulphate ion ($\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$). The catalytic action proceeds via the reduction of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ to $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ by $\text{I}^-$, followed by the oxidation of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ back to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ by $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$. Thus, D matches with II.

The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List IList II
A$n=4, l=3$1$3s$
B$n=5, l=1$2$6d$
C$n=3, l=0$3$4f$
D$n=6, l=2$4$5p$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The principal quantum number $n$ represents the shell and the azimuthal quantum number $l$ represents the subshell.

The subshell notations for different values of $l$ are:
$l = 0 \rightarrow s$
$l = 1 \rightarrow p$
$l = 2 \rightarrow d$
$l = 3 \rightarrow f$

Using these notations:
A: $n=4, l=3$ corresponds to the $4f$ orbital. (A \rightarrow 3)
B: $n=5, l=1$ corresponds to the $5p$ orbital. (B \rightarrow 4)
C: $n=3, l=0$ corresponds to the $3s$ orbital. (C \rightarrow 1)
D: $n=6, l=2$ corresponds to the $6d$ orbital. (D \rightarrow 2)

The correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

Answer: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following combinations of a pentose sugar and a nitrogenous base is exclusively found in the structure of RNA?
questions.solution:
RNA (Ribonucleic acid) is composed of a pentose sugar, phosphoric acid, and nitrogenous bases.

The pentose sugar present in RNA is $\beta$-D-ribose, whereas in DNA it is $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose.

The nitrogenous bases found in RNA are Adenine (A), Guanine (G), Cytosine (C), and Uracil (U). Thymine (T) is found in DNA instead of Uracil.

Therefore, the combination of $\beta$-D-ribose and Uracil is exclusively found in the structure of RNA.

Answer: $\beta$-D-ribose and Uracil

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6][\text{Cr}(\text{CN})_6]$IIonization isomerism
B$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$IICoordination isomerism
C$[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$IIIGeometrical isomerism
D$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+$IVOptical isomerism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
A. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6][\text{Cr}(\text{CN})_6]$ consists of both a complex cation and a complex anion. It exhibits coordination isomerism due to the interchange of ligands between the two coordination spheres.

B. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ exhibits ionization isomerism as it can exchange the coordinated bromide ion with the sulfate counter ion to form $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Br}$.

C. $[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex with three bidentate ligands. It lacks a plane of symmetry and exists as non-superimposable mirror images, thus exhibiting optical isomerism.

D. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_4B_2$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism, existing in cis and trans forms.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the major product formed when $n$-heptane is heated to $773\text{ K}$ at $10-20\text{ atm}$ pressure in the presence of $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ supported over alumina?
questions.solution:
When $n$-heptane is heated to $773\text{ K}$ at $10-20\text{ atm}$ pressure in the presence of a catalyst like $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$, $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$, or $\text{Mo}_2\text{O}_3$ supported over alumina, it undergoes simultaneous dehydrogenation and cyclization. This process is known as aromatization or reforming.

Since $n$-heptane contains seven carbon atoms, it forms a seven-carbon aromatic compound, which is toluene (methylbenzene).

The reaction is:
$\text{CH}_3-(\text{CH}_2)_5-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{V}_2\text{O}_5/\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3, 773\text{ K}, 10-20\text{ atm}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3 + 4\text{H}_2$

Answer: Toluene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An organic compound 'A' with molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ forms an orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent. It is subjected to the chemical tests and reactions shown in the given scheme.

Identify the compounds A and B.
questions.solution:
Compound A ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) forms an orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent, indicating that it is a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone).

It gives a negative Tollens' test, which means it is a ketone, not an aldehyde.

It gives no yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH}$ (negative iodoform test), which means it does not contain a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group (it is not a methyl ketone).

Oxidation of A with $\text{KMnO}_4 / \text{KOH}$ followed by acidification gives Compound B, which produces effervescence with $\text{NaHCO}_3$, indicating that B is a carboxylic acid.

Let us evaluate the given options:
(A) 1-Phenylpropan-2-one ($\text{Ph}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$) is a methyl ketone and would give a positive iodoform test.
(B) 1-Phenylpropan-1-one ($\text{Ph}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) is a ketone (negative Tollens' test) but not a methyl ketone (negative iodoform test). On vigorous oxidation with $\text{KMnO}_4$, it undergoes cleavage to form benzoic acid ($\text{Ph}-\text{COOH}$), which is Compound B. Benzoic acid reacts with $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to give effervescence of $\text{CO}_2$.
(C) 1-(4-Methylphenyl)ethanone is a methyl ketone and would give a positive iodoform test.
(D) 2-Phenylpropanal is an aldehyde and would give a positive Tollens' test.

Therefore, Compound A is 1-Phenylpropan-1-one and Compound B is Benzoic acid.

Answer: A = 1-Phenylpropan-1-one ; B = Benzoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List IList II
A$\text{HCN}$I$5\ \sigma$ bonds
B$\text{XeF}_4$II$3\ \sigma$ bonds, $1\ \pi$ bond
C$\text{PCl}_5$III$4\ \sigma$ bonds, $2$ lone pairs
D$\text{H}_2\text{CO}$IV$2\ \sigma$ bonds, $2\ \pi$ bonds


Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
For $\text{HCN}$, the structure is $\text{H}-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$. It contains $2\ \sigma$ bonds and $2\ \pi$ bonds. Thus, A matches with IV.

For $\text{XeF}_4$, the central atom $\text{Xe}$ has $8$ valence electrons. It forms $4\ \sigma$ bonds with four fluorine atoms and has $2$ lone pairs of electrons. Thus, B matches with III.

For $\text{PCl}_5$, the central atom $\text{P}$ has $5$ valence electrons. It forms $5\ \sigma$ bonds with five chlorine atoms and has no lone pairs. Thus, C matches with I.

For $\text{H}_2\text{CO}$, the structure is $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{O}$. It contains $3\ \sigma$ bonds (two $\text{C}-\text{H}$ and one $\text{C}-\text{O}$) and $1\ \pi$ bond ($\text{C}=\text{O}$). Thus, D matches with II.

The correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequences for 1-bromopropane:
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN (alc.)}} P \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} Q$
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{AgCN (alc.)}} R \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} S$
The major products $Q$ and $S$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
Reaction of 1-bromopropane with alcoholic KCN yields propyl cyanide (butanenitrile) as the major product $P$ because KCN is predominantly ionic, leading to nucleophilic attack through the carbon atom.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{KCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \text{ (P)}$

Reduction of $P$ with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ produces a primary amine, butan-1-amine ($Q$).

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 \text{ (Q)}$

Reaction of 1-bromopropane with alcoholic AgCN yields propyl isocyanide as the major product $R$ because AgCN is predominantly covalent, leading to nucleophilic attack through the nitrogen atom.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{AgCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NC} \text{ (R)}$

Reduction of $R$ with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ produces a secondary amine, N-methylpropan-1-amine ($S$).

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NC} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3 \text{ (S)}$

Thus, $Q$ is butan-1-amine and $S$ is N-methylpropan-1-amine.

Answer: Butan-1-amine and N-Methylpropan-1-amine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of metallic character for the elements N, B, Al, Mg, and K?
questions.solution:
Metallic character is the tendency of an element to lose electrons and form positive ions. It increases down a group and decreases across a period from left to right.

The given elements belong to the following groups and periods:
K: Group 1, Period 4
Mg: Group 2, Period 3
Al: Group 13, Period 3
B: Group 13, Period 2
N: Group 15, Period 2

Potassium (K) is an alkali metal and is the most metallic among the given elements. Magnesium (Mg) is an alkaline earth metal and is more metallic than aluminium (Al), which is a p-block metal. Boron (B) is a metalloid, and nitrogen (N) is a non-metal, making it the least metallic.

Thus, the correct decreasing order of metallic character is $K \gt Mg \gt Al \gt B \gt N$.

Answer: $K \gt Mg \gt Al \gt B \gt N$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the oxidation states of lanthanoids:
I. Europium (Eu) exhibits a $+2$ oxidation state due to the extra stability of the half-filled $4f^{7}$ configuration.
II. Ytterbium (Yb) in its $+2$ oxidation state acts as a strong oxidizing agent in aqueous solutions.
III. Cerium (Ce) exhibits a $+4$ oxidation state and acts as an oxidizing agent, reverting to the common $+3$ state.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of Europium (Eu, $Z=63$) is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{7} 6s^{2}$. By losing two electrons, it forms $\text{Eu}^{2+}$ with a stable half-filled $4f^{7}$ configuration. Thus, Statement I is correct.

The electronic configuration of Ytterbium (Yb, $Z=70$) is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 6s^{2}$. It forms $\text{Yb}^{2+}$ with a fully filled $4f^{14}$ configuration. However, since the $+3$ oxidation state is the most stable state for all lanthanoids, $\text{Yb}^{2+}$ tends to lose an electron to form $\text{Yb}^{3+}$, thereby acting as a reducing agent, not an oxidizing agent. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

The electronic configuration of Cerium (Ce, $Z=58$) is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{1} 5d^{1} 6s^{2}$. It can lose four electrons to achieve a stable noble gas configuration in the $+4$ oxidation state. Since the $+3$ state is more stable, $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ readily accepts an electron to become $\text{Ce}^{3+}$, making it a strong oxidizing agent. Thus, Statement III is correct.

Therefore, only statements I and III are correct.

Answer: I and III only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the following reaction sequence, $X$ and $Z$ respectively are :
$3 \text{CH}_3\text{OH} + \text{PCl}_3 \longrightarrow 3 \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + X$
$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN (alc.)}} Y \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} Z$
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alcohol with phosphorus trichloride ($\text{PCl}_3$) yields an alkyl chloride and phosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$).

$3 \text{CH}_3\text{OH} + \text{PCl}_3 \longrightarrow 3 \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$

Thus, $X$ is $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$.

Methyl chloride undergoes nucleophilic substitution with alcoholic $\text{KCN}$ to form methyl cyanide (acetonitrile).

$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN (alc.)}} \text{CH}_3\text{CN}$

Thus, $Y$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$.

Complete acid hydrolysis of methyl cyanide yields acetic acid.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$

Thus, $Z$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.

Answer: $X = \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$; $Z = \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List IList II
A$[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$IOctahedral
B$[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$IILinear
C$[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$IIITetrahedral
D$[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$IVSquare planar


Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
For $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$, Ni is in the $0$ oxidation state with an electronic configuration of $3d^8 4s^2$. Since CO is a strong field ligand, the $4s$ electrons are forced to pair up in the $3d$ orbitals, resulting in a $3d^{10}$ configuration. The hybridization is $sp^3$, giving a tetrahedral geometry. Thus, A matches III.

For $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in the $+2$ oxidation state with a $3d^8$ configuration. CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, causing the pairing of $3d$ electrons and leaving one $3d$ orbital empty. The hybridization is $dsp^2$, giving a square planar geometry. Thus, B matches IV.

For $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$, Co is in the $+3$ oxidation state. Ethylenediamine (en) is a bidentate ligand, and with three such ligands, the coordination number is $6$. The hybridization is $d^2sp^3$, resulting in an octahedral geometry. Thus, C matches I.

For $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$, Ag is in the $+1$ oxidation state. The coordination number is $2$, which corresponds to $sp$ hybridization and a linear geometry. Thus, D matches II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the correct statements :
A. The molality of $10$ g of glucose (Molar mass : $180$ g mol$^{-1}$) in $250$ g of water is $0.222$ m.
B. The molarity of a solution containing $4.9$ g of $H_2SO_4$ (molar mass : $98$ g mol$^{-1}$) in $500$ mL of solution is $0.1$ M.
C. The solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases with an increase in temperature.
D. Higher the value of Henry's law constant ($K_H$) at a given pressure, higher is the solubility of the gas in the liquid.
E. If $w_A$ and $w_B$ are the masses of components A and B in a binary mixture, the mole fraction of A is given by $x_A = \dfrac{w_A}{w_A + w_B}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A: Molality $m = \dfrac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}} = \dfrac{10 / 180}{250 / 1000} = \dfrac{1}{18} \times 4 = 0.222$ m. Statement A is correct.

Statement B: Molarity $M = \dfrac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Volume of solution in L}} = \dfrac{4.9 / 98}{500 / 1000} = \dfrac{0.05}{0.5} = 0.1$ M. Statement B is correct.

Statement C: Dissolution of a gas in a liquid is an exothermic process. By Le Chatelier's principle, the solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases with an increase in temperature. Statement C is correct.

Statement D: According to Henry's law, $p = K_H x \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{p}{K_H}$. At a given pressure, a higher value of $K_H$ implies a lower solubility $x$. Statement D is incorrect.

Statement E: Mole fraction is the ratio of moles, not masses. $x_A = \dfrac{n_A}{n_A + n_B}$. The given formula represents mass fraction. Statement E is incorrect.

The correct statements are A, B, and C.

Answer: A, B and C only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During the qualitative analysis of an inorganic salt, the addition of dilute $\text{HCl}$ produces a colourless gas with a highly offensive smell resembling rotten eggs. Furthermore, this gas turns a filter paper moistened with lead acetate solution black. Identify the anion present in the salt.
questions.solution:
When dilute $\text{HCl}$ is added to a salt containing a sulphide ion ($\text{S}^{2-}$), hydrogen sulphide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$) gas is evolved.

$\text{S}^{2-} + 2\text{H}^{+} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{S} \uparrow$

Hydrogen sulphide is a colourless gas with a characteristic rotten egg smell. When it comes in contact with lead acetate, it forms a black precipitate of lead sulphide ($\text{PbS}$).

$\text{H}_2\text{S} + \text{Pb}(\text{CH}_3\text{COO})_2 \rightarrow \text{PbS} \downarrow + 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$

Thus, the anion present in the salt is sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$).

Answer: Sulphide, $\text{S}^{2-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the reduction potential of the half-cell given below at $298\text{ K}$:
$\text{Pt(s)} | \text{Cl}_2\text{(g, 9 atm)} | \text{Cl}^-\text{(aq, 0.03 M)}$
Given: $E^{\circ}_{\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-} = 1.36\text{ V}$
$\left(\text{Assume } \dfrac{2.303\ RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\right)$
questions.solution:
The reduction half-reaction for the given chlorine electrode is:

$\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} + 2e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}^-\text{(aq)}$

The Nernst equation for the reduction potential is given by:

$E = E^{\circ} - \dfrac{0.059}{n} \log \dfrac{[\text{Cl}^-]^2}{P_{\text{Cl}_2}}$

Here, the number of electrons transferred is $n = 2$. Substituting the given values:

$E = 1.36 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \log \dfrac{(0.03)^2}{9}$

$E = 1.36 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \log \dfrac{9 \times 10^{-4}}{9}$

$E = 1.36 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \log (10^{-4})$

$E = 1.36 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \times (-4)$

$E = 1.36 + 0.118$

$E = 1.478\text{ V}$

Answer: $1.478\text{ V}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of a transition metal ion exhibits a spin-only magnetic moment of $5.92\text{ BM}$. The ion could be :
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 5.92\text{ BM}$, we have $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 5.92$.

Squaring both sides gives $n(n+2) \approx 35$, which yields $n = 5$.

The electronic configurations of the given ions are:

$\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($Z=26$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$, which has $4$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($Z=28$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$, which has $2$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($Z=25$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5$, which has $5$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Ti}^{3+}$ ($Z=22$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^1$, which has $1$ unpaired electron.

Since $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ has $5$ unpaired electrons, it exhibits a spin-only magnetic moment of $5.92\text{ BM}$.

Answer: $\text{Mn}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding Group 14 elements and their allotropes is incorrect?
options: Carbon cannot expand its coordination number beyond four due to the absence of $d$-orbitals in its valence shell.
The heavier elements of this group do not readily form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with themselves.
Diamond is the most thermodynamically stable allotrope of carbon at standard temperature and pressure.
The relative stability of the $+2$ oxidation state increases down the group from Germanium to Lead.
questions.solution:
Carbon cannot expand its coordination number beyond four because it lacks $d$-orbitals in its valence shell. This makes the first statement correct.

Heavier elements of Group 14 (like Si, Ge, Sn, Pb) have larger atomic sizes, which results in diffuse $p$-orbitals. This prevents effective lateral overlap, so they do not readily form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with themselves. This makes the second statement correct.

Graphite is the most thermodynamically stable allotrope of carbon at standard temperature and pressure, not diamond. The standard enthalpy of formation of graphite is taken as zero, whereas for diamond it is $1.90 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. This makes the third statement incorrect.

Due to the inert pair effect, the $ns^2$ electrons become increasingly reluctant to participate in bonding down the group. Consequently, the relative stability of the $+2$ oxidation state increases from Germanium to Lead. This makes the fourth statement correct.

Answer: Diamond is the most thermodynamically stable allotrope of carbon at standard temperature and pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The temperature dependence of the rate constant for the decomposition of a gaseous hydrocarbon is given by the following equation:
$\log k = 12.5 - \dfrac{4200}{T}$
What is the activation energy ($E_a$) for this reaction in kJ mol$^{-1}$?
(Given: $R = 8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, $2.303 \times 8.314 = 19.15$)
questions.solution:
The Arrhenius equation is given by:

$\log k = \log A - \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 RT}$

The given equation is:

$\log k = 12.5 - \dfrac{4200}{T}$

Comparing the two equations, we get:

$\dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} = 4200$

$E_a = 4200 \times 2.303 \times R$

Substituting $R = 8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$:

$E_a = 4200 \times 2.303 \times 8.314$

Given $2.303 \times 8.314 = 19.15$:

$E_a = 4200 \times 19.15 = 80430$ J mol$^{-1}$

$E_a = 80.43$ kJ mol$^{-1}$

Answer: $80.43$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the condition of ovules in gymnosperms?
options: They are enclosed by an ovary wall before fertilization but become exposed later.
They are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization.
They are completely enclosed within a fruit post-fertilization.
They remain exposed before fertilization but are covered by a fleshy pericarp after fertilization.
questions.solution:
Gymnosperms (gymnos = naked, sperma = seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization.

The seeds that develop post-fertilization are not covered, i.e., they are naked.

Therefore, the statement that they are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization is correct.

Answer: They are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements regarding the reasons for biodiversity conservation:

Statement I: The narrowly utilitarian arguments for conserving biodiversity are based on the countless direct economic benefits humans derive from nature, such as food, firewood, fibre, and medicinal products.
Statement II: The broadly utilitarian argument for conserving biodiversity relates to the realisation that every species has an intrinsic value, even if it may not be of current economic value to us.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
The narrowly utilitarian arguments for conserving biodiversity are based on the direct economic benefits humans derive from nature, such as food, firewood, fibre, construction material, industrial products, and medicinal products. Thus, Statement I is correct.

The broadly utilitarian argument says that biodiversity plays a major role in many ecosystem services that nature provides, such as oxygen production, pollination, and aesthetic pleasures. The realisation that every species has an intrinsic value, even if it may not be of current economic value to us, forms the basis of the ethical argument for conserving biodiversity, not the broadly utilitarian argument. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

Chitinase is an enzyme used to break open fungal cells, as their cell walls are made of chitin. Thus, B matches with 4.

DNA ligase is an enzyme that facilitates the joining of DNA strands together by catalyzing the formation of a phosphodiester bond. Thus, C matches with 2.

Lysozyme is an enzyme used to break open bacterial cells by degrading the peptidoglycan in their cell walls. Thus, D matches with 1.

The correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1.

Answer: A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
APrimary production1$kcal \cdot m^{-2} \cdot yr^{-1}$
BPrimary productivity2$kcal \cdot m^{-2}$
CAnnual NPP of whole biosphere355 billion tons
DAnnual NPP of oceans4170 billion tons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Primary production is the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed in terms of weight ($g \cdot m^{-2}$) or energy ($kcal \cdot m^{-2}$).

Primary productivity is the rate of biomass production. It is expressed in terms of $g \cdot m^{-2} \cdot yr^{-1}$ or $kcal \cdot m^{-2} \cdot yr^{-1}$.

The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter.

The annual net primary productivity of oceans is 55 billion tons.

Thus, the correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

Answer: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The ongoing 'Sixth Extinction' episode is fundamentally different from the previous five mass extinctions that Earth has witnessed since the origin of life.
Reason (R): The current species extinction rates are estimated to be $100$ to $1000$ times faster than in pre-human times, primarily driven by anthropogenic activities.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
During the long period since the origin and diversification of life on Earth, there have been five episodes of mass extinction of species.

The ongoing 'Sixth Extinction' is fundamentally different from the previous episodes. The primary difference lies in the rate of extinction.

The current species extinction rates are estimated to be $100$ to $1000$ times faster than in pre-human times. This accelerated rate is primarily driven by anthropogenic (human) activities, such as habitat destruction, overexploitation, pollution, and the introduction of exotic species.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Adult human haemoglobin consists of four polypeptide subunits (two $\alpha$ and two $\beta$ type). This assembly represents which level of protein structure?
questions.solution:
Adult human haemoglobin is composed of four polypeptide subunits, specifically two $\alpha$ and two $\beta$ chains.

The primary structure refers to the linear sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide chain.

The secondary structure refers to the local folding of the polypeptide chain into structures such as $\alpha$-helices and $\beta$-pleated sheets.

The tertiary structure is the overall three-dimensional shape of a single polypeptide chain.

The quaternary structure is the spatial arrangement and interaction of multiple polypeptide subunits to form a functional protein complex.

Since haemoglobin consists of multiple (four) subunits interacting together, it represents the quaternary level of protein structure.

Answer: Quaternary structure

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the bulliform cells found in isobilateral leaves?
options: They are modified abaxial epidermal cells containing abundant chloroplasts.
When they become turgid, they cause the leaf to curl inwards to prevent water loss.
They are large, empty, colourless cells present on the adaxial epidermis along the veins.
They are specialized bundle sheath cells that regulate the transport of water and minerals.
questions.solution:
In grasses (isobilateral leaves), certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells known as bulliform cells.

When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

Therefore, they are large, empty, colourless cells present on the adaxial epidermis along the veins.

Answer: They are large, empty, colourless cells present on the adaxial epidermis along the veins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During the amplification of a gene of interest using Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the reaction mixture is briefly cooled to approximately $50^{\circ}\text{C} - 60^{\circ}\text{C}$ after an initial high-temperature treatment. Which of the following events takes place during this cooling phase?
options: Separation of the double-stranded template DNA into single strands
Hybridization of oligonucleotide primers to the complementary regions of the template DNA
Addition of deoxynucleotides to the primer by a thermostable DNA polymerase
Ligation of the newly synthesized DNA fragments to form a continuous strand
questions.solution:
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) involves three main steps:

1. Denaturation: The reaction mixture is heated to $94^{\circ}\text{C} - 96^{\circ}\text{C}$ to separate the double-stranded DNA into single strands.

2. Annealing: The mixture is cooled to $50^{\circ}\text{C} - 60^{\circ}\text{C}$. This allows the oligonucleotide primers to hybridize (anneal) to their complementary sequences on the single-stranded template DNA.

3. Extension: The temperature is raised to $72^{\circ}\text{C}$, allowing a thermostable DNA polymerase (like Taq polymerase) to add deoxynucleotides to the primers, synthesizing the new DNA strand.

The cooling phase corresponds to the annealing step, where primers hybridize to the template DNA.

Answer: Hybridization of oligonucleotide primers to the complementary regions of the template DNA

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List IList II
A$G_1$ phase1Centriole duplication in the cytoplasm
BS phase2Inactive stage where cells do not proliferate
C$G_2$ phase3Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication
D$G_0$ phase4Proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis


Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$G_1$ phase is the interval between mitosis and the initiation of DNA replication. The cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.

S phase or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.

During the $G_2$ phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

Cells that do not divide further exit the $G_1$ phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage ($G_0$) of the cell cycle. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2.

Answer: A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the causes of biodiversity loss:
A. The illegal introduction of the African catfish ($Clariasgariepinus$) for aquaculture purposes poses a threat to indigenous catfishes.
B. Mammals and birds requiring large territories are generally unaffected by habitat fragmentation.
C. Over-exploitation of marine fish populations around the world is endangering the continued existence of some commercially important species.
D. In an obligate plant-pollinator mutualism, the extinction of one invariably leads to the extinction of the other.
E. $Parthenium$ and $Lantana$ are examples of native species that promote the growth of indigenous plants.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct as the illegal introduction of the African catfish ($Clariasgariepinus$) is an example of alien species invasion which threatens indigenous catfishes.

Statement B is incorrect because mammals and birds requiring large territories are severely affected by habitat fragmentation, leading to population declines.

Statement C is correct as over-exploitation of marine fish populations endangers the continued existence of many commercially important species.

Statement D is correct because in an obligate plant-pollinator mutualism, the extinction of one species inevitably leads to the co-extinction of the other.

Statement E is incorrect as $Parthenium$ and $Lantana$ are invasive alien weed species, not native, and they pose a threat to indigenous plants rather than promoting their growth.

Therefore, statements A, C, and D are correct.

Answer: A, C and D only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the strands of a transcription unit ?
A. DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in the $3' \rightarrow 5'$ direction.
B. The DNA strand with $3' \rightarrow 5'$ polarity acts as the template strand.
C. The strand which does not code for anything during transcription is referred to as the coding strand.
D. All reference points while defining a transcription unit are made with respect to the template strand.
E. By switching the position of the promoter with the terminator, the definition of coding and template strands could be reversed.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect because DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization only in one direction, which is $5' \rightarrow 3'$.

Statement B is correct because the DNA strand with $3' \rightarrow 5'$ polarity acts as the template for transcription, as RNA synthesis occurs in the $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction.

Statement C is correct because the strand with $5' \rightarrow 3'$ polarity, which has the same sequence as the newly synthesized RNA (except thymine instead of uracil), is called the coding strand, even though it does not code for anything during transcription.

Statement D is incorrect because all reference points while defining a transcription unit are made with respect to the coding strand, not the template strand.

Statement E is correct because the promoter defines the template and coding strands. By switching the position of the promoter with the terminator, the direction of transcription is reversed, which reverses the definition of the coding and template strands.

Therefore, statements B, C, and E are correct.

Answer: B, C and E only

BLeaching2Precipitation of water-soluble inorganic nutrients as unavailable salts in the soil horizon

questions.solution:
Fragmentation is the process in which detritivores (like earthworms) break down detritus into smaller particles. Thus, A matches with 4.

Leaching is the process by which water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts. Thus, B matches with 2.

Catabolism involves bacterial and fungal enzymes degrading detritus into simpler inorganic substances. Thus, C matches with 1.

Humus is a dark-coloured, highly resistant amorphous substance that undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate. Thus, D matches with 3.

The correct matching is A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.

Answer: A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3

questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

BCo-dominance2More than two alleles govern the same character
CPleiotropy3F$_{1}$ generation resembles both the parents
DMultiple alleles4F$_{1}$ generation is in between the two parents

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Incomplete dominance occurs when the F$_{1}$ generation has a phenotype that is intermediate between the two parents.

Co-dominance occurs when the F$_{1}$ generation resembles both parents, as both alleles express themselves fully.

Pleiotropy is the phenomenon where a single gene exhibits multiple phenotypic expressions.

Multiple alleles refer to the condition where more than two alleles govern the same character.

Thus, the correct matching is A-4, B-3, C-1, D-2.

Answer: A-4, B-3, C-1, D-2

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the packaging of DNA helix in eukaryotes?
A. A typical nucleosome contains 200 bp of DNA helix.
B. The 'beads-on-string' structure in chromatin is clearly seen when viewed under a light microscope.
C. Chromatin fibres are further coiled and condensed at metaphase stage of cell division to form chromosomes.
D. Euchromatin is densely packed and stains dark.
E. Euchromatin is said to be transcriptionally active chromatin, whereas heterochromatin is inactive.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. A typical nucleosome contains about $200$ bp of DNA helix wrapped around the histone octamer.

Statement B is incorrect. The 'beads-on-string' structure in chromatin is observed under an electron microscope, not a light microscope.

Statement C is correct. Chromatin fibres are further coiled and condensed at the metaphase stage of cell division to form chromosomes.

Statement D is incorrect. Euchromatin is loosely packed and stains light, whereas heterochromatin is densely packed and stains dark.

Statement E is correct. Euchromatin is transcriptionally active chromatin, whereas heterochromatin is transcriptionally inactive.

Therefore, statements A, C, and E are correct.

Answer: A, C and E only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Identify the correct statement(s) regarding the mechanism of light reaction in photosynthesis :
A. In a photosystem, a single chlorophyll a molecule forms the reaction centre.
B. Cyclic photophosphorylation occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond 680 nm are available for excitation.
C. The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the lumen side of the thylakoid membrane.
D. The breakdown of the proton gradient provides energy to cause a conformational change in the $\text{CF}_0$ particle of the ATP synthase.
E. The splitting of water is associated with PS II and occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. In a photosystem, the reaction centre is formed by a single chlorophyll a molecule.

Statement B is correct. Cyclic photophosphorylation occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond $680\text{ nm}$ are available for excitation, as only PS I is functional.

Statement C is incorrect. The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane, not the lumen side.

Statement D is incorrect. The breakdown of the proton gradient provides energy to cause a conformational change in the $\text{CF}_1$ particle of the ATP synthase, not the $\text{CF}_0$ particle.

Statement E is correct. The splitting of water is associated with PS II and occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.

Therefore, statements A, B, and E are correct.

Answer: A, B and E only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
AStele1Large, empty, colourless cells in grasses
BPericycle2Ground tissue of leaf possessing chloroplasts
CBulliform cells3All tissues on the inner side of endodermis
DMesophyll4Site of initiation of lateral roots

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Stele comprises all the tissues present on the inner side of the endodermis, which includes the pericycle, vascular bundles, and pith. Thus, A matches 3.

Pericycle is the layer of cells just inside the endodermis. In roots, the initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during secondary growth takes place in the pericycle cells. Thus, B matches 4.

Bulliform cells are large, empty, colourless cells found in the adaxial epidermis of grasses (monocots) along the veins. They help in the rolling and unrolling of leaves to minimize water loss. Thus, C matches 1.

Mesophyll is the ground tissue of leaves located between the upper and lower epidermis. It contains chloroplasts and is responsible for photosynthesis. Thus, D matches 2.

The correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

Answer: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the different phases of plant growth is correct?
options: Cells in the zone of elongation are characterized by a rich protoplasm and large conspicuous nuclei.
The zone of maturation lies distal to the zone of elongation in a growing root apex.
Cells in the meristematic phase possess primary, thin, and cellulosic cell walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.
The cells in the elongation phase attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.
questions.solution:
The period of growth is generally divided into three phases: meristematic, elongation, and maturation.

The constantly dividing cells, both at the root apex and the shoot apex, represent the meristematic phase of growth. The cells in this region are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei, and their cell walls are primary in nature, thin, and cellulosic with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

The cells proximal (just next, away from the tip) to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in this phase.

Further away from the apex, i.e., more proximal to the phase of elongation, lies the portion of axis which is undergoing the phase of maturation. The cells of this zone attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.

Answer: Cells in the meristematic phase possess primary, thin, and cellulosic cell walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List IList II

BAuxin2Promotes rapid internode elongation in deep water rice plants
CCytokinin3Promotes bolting in rosette plants
DGibberellin4Helps overcome apical dominance

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Ethylene promotes rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants, helping the leaves or upper parts of the shoot to remain above water. Thus, A matches with 2.

Auxins are widely used in agriculture and horticulture to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, which is useful for plant propagation. Thus, B matches with 1.

Cytokinins promote lateral shoot growth and help overcome apical dominance. Thus, C matches with 4.

Gibberellins promote bolting, which is internode elongation just prior to flowering, in rosette plants like beet and cabbage. Thus, D matches with 3.

The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

Answer: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the enzymes used in recombinant DNA technology and identify the incorrect statements.
A. Exonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.
B. A restriction endonuclease inspects the length of a DNA sequence to find its specific recognition sequence.
C. EcoRI cuts the DNA between bases G and A only when the sequence GAATTC is present in the DNA.
D. DNA ligase joins the two DNA molecules by forming hydrogen bonds between the sticky ends.
E. The first restriction endonuclease whose functioning depended on a specific DNA nucleotide sequence was Hind II.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect because exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA, whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.

Statement B is correct as each restriction endonuclease functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence to find its specific recognition sequence.

Statement C is correct because EcoRI specifically recognizes the palindromic sequence GAATTC and cuts the DNA between the bases G and A.

Statement D is incorrect because DNA ligase joins two DNA molecules by forming phosphodiester bonds between adjacent nucleotides of the sugar-phosphate backbone, not by forming hydrogen bonds. Hydrogen bonds between sticky ends form spontaneously due to complementary base pairing.

Statement E is correct as Hind II was the first restriction endonuclease to be discovered and its functioning depended on a specific DNA nucleotide sequence.

Therefore, the incorrect statements are A and D.

Answer: A and D only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Identify the correct statements regarding biomolecules.
A. Amino acids are substituted methanes.
B. Palmitic acid contains 16 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon.
C. Uracil is a purine nitrogenous base present in RNA.
D. Cellulose is a heteropolymer consisting of multiple types of monosaccharides.
E. Dietary proteins are the source of essential amino acids for our body.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct as amino acids are organic compounds containing an amino group and an acidic group as substituents on the same $\alpha$-carbon, making them substituted methanes.

Statement B is correct as palmitic acid is a saturated fatty acid with the formula $CH_3(CH_2)_{14}COOH$, which contains a total of 16 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon.

Statement C is incorrect because uracil is a pyrimidine nitrogenous base, not a purine. Purines include adenine and guanine.

Statement D is incorrect because cellulose is a homopolymer made up of only one type of monosaccharide, which is glucose.

Statement E is correct as essential amino acids cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through dietary proteins.

Thus, the correct statements are A, B, and E.

Answer: A, B and E only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the chromosomal mechanism of sex determination in certain insects like honeybees:
A. The sex of the offspring is determined by the number of sets of chromosomes it receives.
B. Gametogenesis in males occurs through equational division.
C. A male individual in this system lacks a father and cannot produce sons.
D. The females possess 16 chromosomes while the males possess 32 chromosomes.
E. Males inherit their genetic material from both parents.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E only
questions.solution:
In the haplodiploid sex determination system found in honeybees, the sex of the offspring is determined by the number of sets of chromosomes it receives. Fertilized eggs develop into diploid females, while unfertilized eggs develop into haploid males (drones) by parthenogenesis. Thus, statement A is correct.

Since males are haploid, they produce sperms by mitosis, which is an equational division. Thus, statement B is correct.

Because males develop from unfertilized eggs, they do not have a father. Furthermore, since they only contribute their genetics to female offspring (fertilized eggs), they cannot have sons. Thus, statement C is correct.

Females are diploid and possess $32$ chromosomes, whereas males are haploid and possess $16$ chromosomes. Thus, statement D is incorrect.

Males inherit their genetic material only from their mother, not from both parents. Thus, statement E is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements A, B, and C are correct.

Answer: A, B and C only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding amino acids?
A. The R group in the amino acid alanine is a methyl group.
B. Tyrosine, phenylalanine and tryptophan are aromatic amino acids.
C. Glutamic acid is an example of a basic amino acid.
D. The R group in glycine is a hydroxymethyl group.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. The R group in alanine is a methyl group ($-CH_3$).

Statement B is correct. Tyrosine, phenylalanine, and tryptophan contain aromatic rings in their side chains, making them aromatic amino acids.

Statement C is incorrect. Glutamic acid contains an extra carboxyl group in its side chain, making it an acidic amino acid, not a basic one.

Statement D is incorrect. The R group in glycine is a hydrogen atom ($-H$), making it the simplest amino acid. The amino acid with a hydroxymethyl group ($-CH_2OH$) as its R group is serine.

Therefore, only statements A and B are correct.

Answer: A and B only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
AGlucose \rightarrow Glucose-6-phosphateISplitting of a 6-carbon compound
BFructose-1,6-bisphosphate \rightarrow Triose phosphateIIRelease of a water molecule
C2-Phosphoglycerate \rightarrow PhosphoenolpyruvateIIIGeneration of ATP
DPhosphoenolpyruvate \rightarrow Pyruvic acidIVConsumption of ATP

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
In the process of glycolysis:

A. Glucose \rightarrow Glucose-6-phosphate: This is the first step of glycolysis, catalyzed by the enzyme hexokinase. In this step, one molecule of ATP is consumed to phosphorylate glucose. Thus, A matches with IV.

B. Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate \rightarrow Triose phosphate: The 6-carbon compound fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is split into two 3-carbon compounds (glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate and dihydroxyacetone phosphate) by the enzyme aldolase. Thus, B matches with I.

C. 2-Phosphoglycerate \rightarrow Phosphoenolpyruvate: This step is catalyzed by enolase and involves the removal of a water molecule (dehydration) to form a double bond. Thus, C matches with II.

D. Phosphoenolpyruvate \rightarrow Pyruvic acid: This is the final step of glycolysis, catalyzed by pyruvate kinase. A phosphate group is transferred from phosphoenolpyruvate to ADP, generating ATP. Thus, D matches with III.

The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
AFree central1Ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part
BParietal2Placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary
CBasal3Ovules are borne on central axis and septa are absent
DMarginal4Placenta develops at the base of ovary and a single ovule is attached

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Free central placentation: Ovules are borne on the central axis and septa are absent, as seen in Dianthus and Primrose. (A \rightarrow 3)

Parietal placentation: Ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on the peripheral part, as seen in mustard and Argemone. (B \rightarrow 1)

Basal placentation: Placenta develops at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it, as seen in sunflower and marigold. (C \rightarrow 4)

Marginal placentation: Placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and ovules are borne on this ridge, as seen in pea. (D \rightarrow 2)

The correct matching is A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2.

Answer: A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the enzymes used in recombinant DNA technology:
A. Restriction endonucleases cut the sugar-phosphate backbone of both DNA strands at specific points.
B. EcoRI cuts the DNA between bases C and T only when the sequence GAATTC is present in the DNA.
C. The Roman numbers following the name of a restriction enzyme indicate the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain of bacteria.
D. Exonucleases remove nucleotides from specific positions within the DNA.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. Restriction endonucleases function by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence and binding to specific recognition sequences, where they cut the sugar-phosphate backbone of both DNA strands at specific points.

Statement B is incorrect. The restriction enzyme EcoRI recognizes the palindromic sequence GAATTC and cuts the DNA between the bases G and A, not between C and T.

Statement C is correct. In the nomenclature of restriction enzymes, the Roman numerals following the name indicate the order in which the enzymes were isolated from that particular strain of bacteria.

Statement D is incorrect. Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA molecule, whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.

Therefore, only statements A and C are correct.

Answer: A and C only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome linked recessive trait. At the molecular level, this disorder is caused by a single base substitution at the sixth codon of the $\beta$-globin gene. Which of the following represents the correct change in the mRNA codon?
questions.solution:
Sickle-cell anaemia is caused by a point mutation at the sixth position of the $\beta$-globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule.

The mutation involves a single base substitution in the DNA, where the CTC codon on the template strand is changed to CAC.

This results in a change in the mRNA codon from GAG to GUG.

Consequently, the amino acid glutamic acid (Glu) is replaced by valine (Val) at the sixth position of the $\beta$-globin chain.

Therefore, the correct change in the mRNA codon is GAG \rightarrow GUG.

Answer: GAG \rightarrow GUG

questions.subject: Biology

Match List I with List II :

BAndrogenic steroids2Stimulates the formation of red blood cells
CCatecholamines3Stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis
DErythropoietin4Play a role in the growth of axial hair and pubic hair


Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular uptake and utilization of amino acids.

Androgenic steroids secreted by the adrenal cortex play a role in the growth of axial hair, pubic hair, and facial hair during puberty.

Catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline) increase the heart beat, the strength of heart contraction, and the rate of respiration.

Erythropoietin is a peptide hormone produced by the juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney which stimulates erythropoiesis (formation of red blood cells).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

Answer: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Arrange the following events occurring during the regulation of kidney function by the hypothalamus in the correct order :
A. ADH facilitates water reabsorption from latter parts of the tubule.
B. Osmoreceptors are switched off and ADH release is suppressed.
C. Excessive loss of fluid from the body activates osmoreceptors.
D. Prevention of diuresis and increase in body fluid volume.
E. Hypothalamus is stimulated to release ADH from the neurohypophysis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Excessive loss of fluid from the body activates osmoreceptors in the body (C).

These activated receptors stimulate the hypothalamus to release antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or vasopressin from the neurohypophysis (E).

ADH facilitates water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule (A).

This reabsorption prevents diuresis and leads to an increase in body fluid volume (D).

The increase in body fluid volume switches off the osmoreceptors and suppresses ADH release to complete the feedback loop (B).

The correct sequence of events is C, E, A, D, B.

Answer: C, E, A, D, B

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Observe the schematic representation of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction given below:

Identify the class to which enzyme 'E' belongs according to the standard enzyme classification.
questions.solution:
The given schematic representation shows the joining of two molecules, $A$ and $B$, to form a new compound $A-B$.

This bond formation is coupled with the hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and inorganic phosphate ($P_i$), which provides the necessary energy for the reaction.

According to the standard enzyme classification, enzymes that catalyze the linking together of two compounds, typically driven by the breakdown of a pyrophosphate bond in ATP or a similar compound, belong to the class Ligases.

Therefore, the enzyme 'E' is a ligase.

Answer: Ligases

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List IList II
AInspiratory Capacity (IC)1TV + ERV
BExpiratory Capacity (EC)2ERV + RV
CFunctional Residual Capacity (FRC)3ERV + TV + IRV
DVital Capacity (VC)4TV + IRV

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Inspiratory Capacity (IC) is the total volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration. It includes tidal volume and inspiratory reserve volume. Thus, IC = TV + IRV.

Expiratory Capacity (EC) is the total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration. It includes tidal volume and expiratory reserve volume. Thus, EC = TV + ERV.

Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is the volume of air that remains in the lungs after a normal expiration. It includes expiratory reserve volume and residual volume. Thus, FRC = ERV + RV.

Vital Capacity (VC) is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration or breathe out after a forced inspiration. It includes expiratory reserve volume, tidal volume, and inspiratory reserve volume. Thus, VC = ERV + TV + IRV.

The correct matching is A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3.

Answer: A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the morphology of the Indian bullfrog (Rana tigrina) :
A. The body is divisible into head, neck and trunk.
B. The skin is smooth and slippery due to the presence of mucus.
C. Forelimbs end in five digits while hind limbs end in four digits.
D. On either side of the eyes, a membranous tympanum receives sound signals.
E. The skin on the ventral side of the body is uniformly pale yellow.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The body of a frog is divisible into head and trunk. A neck and tail are absent, making statement A incorrect.

The skin of a frog is smooth and slippery due to the presence of mucus, making statement B correct.

The forelimbs of a frog end in four digits while the hind limbs end in five digits, making statement C incorrect.

On either side of the eyes, a membranous tympanum (ear) is present which receives sound signals, making statement D correct.

The colour of the dorsal side of the body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots, while the skin on the ventral side is uniformly pale yellow, making statement E correct.

Therefore, statements B, D, and E are correct.

Answer: B, D and E only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II with respect to the chronology of evolutionary events :

BAbout $2000$ mya2Primates called Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus existed
CAbout $200$ mya3First non-cellular forms of life originated

questions.solution:

First non-cellular forms of life originated about $3$ billion years ago. They would have been giant molecules like RNA, proteins, and polysaccharides.

The first cellular forms of life appeared about $2000$ million years ago (mya).

About $200$ mya, some land reptiles went back into the water to evolve into fish-like reptiles (e.g., Ichthyosaurs).

About $15$ mya, primates called Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus existed.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following sets of animals belong exclusively to the class Chondrichthyes?
options: Saw fish, Dog fish and Sea horse
Electric ray, Stingray and Great white shark
Flying fish, Magur and Saw fish
questions.solution:
Electric ray (Torpedo), Stingray (Trygon), and Great white shark (Carcharodon) are all cartilaginous fishes belonging to the class Chondrichthyes.

In the other options:
Sea horse (Hippocampus) belongs to Osteichthyes.
Lamprey (Petromyzon) and Hagfish (Myxine) belong to Cyclostomata.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Select the incorrect statements from the following :
A. In sponges, cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, exhibiting a cellular level of organisation.
B. Radial symmetry is observed in the members of phyla Platyhelminthes and Aschelminthes.
C. Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs and Chordates are coelomate animals.
D. Notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the ventral side during embryonic development.
E. Mesoglea is an undifferentiated layer present between the ectoderm and endoderm in diploblastic animals.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct as sponges exhibit a cellular level of organisation with cells arranged as loose aggregates.

Statement B is incorrect because members of phyla Platyhelminthes and Aschelminthes exhibit bilateral symmetry, not radial symmetry. Radial symmetry is found in Coelenterates, Ctenophores, and adult Echinoderms.

Statement C is correct as Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs, and Chordates possess a true coelom and are thus coelomate animals.

Statement D is incorrect because the notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the dorsal side, not the ventral side, during embryonic development in some animals.

Statement E is correct as mesoglea is an undifferentiated layer present between the ectoderm and endoderm in diploblastic animals.

Therefore, the incorrect statements are B and D.

Answer: B and D only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the Rh blood group system and select the incorrect ones:
A. The Rh antigen, similar to one present in Rhesus monkeys, is found on the surface of RBCs in nearly 80 per cent of humans.
B. An Rh$^{-ve}$ person, if exposed to Rh$^{+ve}$ blood, will form specific antibodies against the Rh antigens.
C. In Rh incompatibility during pregnancy, the maternal blood is normally well separated from the fetal blood by the placenta during the first pregnancy.
D. Erythroblastosis foetalis is characterized by severe anaemia and jaundice in the pregnant mother due to the destruction of her RBCs.
E. To prevent erythroblastosis foetalis, anti-Rh antibodies are administered to the Rh$^{+ve}$ mother immediately after the delivery of her first child.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct as the Rh antigen is present on the surface of RBCs in nearly 80 per cent of humans.

Statement B is correct as exposure of Rh$^{-ve}$ blood to Rh$^{+ve}$ blood induces the formation of specific anti-Rh antibodies.

Statement C is correct because during the first pregnancy, maternal and foetal blood are well separated by the placenta, preventing mixing.

Statement D is incorrect because erythroblastosis foetalis causes severe anaemia and jaundice in the foetus, not in the pregnant mother. The maternal antibodies cross the placenta and destroy the foetal RBCs.

Statement E is incorrect because anti-Rh antibodies are administered to an Rh$^{-ve}$ mother (not an Rh$^{+ve}$ mother) immediately after the delivery of her first Rh$^{+ve}$ child to prevent erythroblastosis foetalis in subsequent pregnancies.

Thus, statements D and E are incorrect.

Answer: D and E only
